methodology: Authorized external service discovery, banner fingerprinting, and exposure classification against a client-approved scope.

vulnerabilities.title: Database service exposed to the public internet
vulnerabilities.description: A MySQL database service on port 3306 is reachable from the public internet. Database services should never be directly exposed; they are a primary target for credential-stuffing and known-CVE exploitation.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Restrict port 3306 to trusted internal hosts or a VPN using a firewall/security group. If remote access is required, place the database behind a bastion or SSH tunnel and never bind it to 0.0.0.0.
vulnerabilities.evidence: TCP connect to 203.0.113.10:3306 returned MySQL handshake banner 5.7.33.

vulnerabilities.title: Outdated SSH server version
vulnerabilities.description: The SSH banner reports OpenSSH 7.4, released in 2016. Multiple vulnerabilities have been disclosed against this branch. Running end-of-life SSH increases the risk of compromise.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Upgrade OpenSSH to the current stable release provided by your OS vendor and enable automatic security updates. Disable password authentication in favor of keys.

vulnerabilities.title: HTTP served without redirect to HTTPS
vulnerabilities.description: The web server responds on plain HTTP (port 80) without redirecting to HTTPS. Traffic on port 80 is unencrypted and can be intercepted or modified in transit.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Configure a 301 redirect from HTTP to HTTPS and enable HSTS with a long max-age. Obtain a free certificate via Let's Encrypt if one is not already in place.
vulnerabilities.evidence: GET / on port 80 returned 200 OK with no Location redirect header.
